title: HTTP/3 RFC 9114 Positive Floor Architecture
purpose: Define the implementation boundary for HTTP/3 frame handling, stream classification, SETTINGS exchange, header validation, and the minimal client/server request-response floor over the managed QUIC transport.
design_summary: The HTTP/3 package owns deterministic frame parsing and writing, stream classification, control-stream sequencing, SETTINGS exchange, header validation, and the minimal request/response floor. These behaviors are implemented against Incursa.Quic and QPACK. Malformed-sequence handling remains separately traced so the positive floor and negative protocol tests stay auditable without conflating them. ASP.NET hosting remains out of scope.
data_and_state_considerations: The frame reader retains partial bytes until enough input arrives, the stream dispatcher tracks stream kind and one-time control-stream registration, SETTINGS exchange writes once and captures the peer settings once, and the request/response validators preserve header ordering, content-length accounting, and message sequencing state. These states are deterministic and must fail with stable HTTP/3 error mapping when input is malformed.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Frame parsing must tolerate partial buffers and reject truncated or overrun frames deterministically.
Unknown and reserved frame types must remain representable as unknown frames when the stream permits them.
Only one control stream may exist per endpoint, and SETTINGS must be the first frame on that stream.
Request and response header validation must reject pseudo-header order violations, uppercase field names, and connection-specific fields.
The minimal client/server floor must use QPACK for headers while keeping the HTTP/3 package independent from ASP.NET hosting.
risks: The HTTP/3 package can be mistaken for application hosting or for the external peer harness; those concerns remain separate.
The positive floor must not be conflated with interop matrix completeness or with the standalone QPACK codec ownership.
Future features such as broader application hosting remain separate from the protocol floor traced here.

supplemental_sections.heading: Positive Floor Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This artifact covers the HTTP/3 runtime floor already exercised by loopback tests. It does not introduce ASP.NET integration requirements or external peer-specific behavior beyond the protocol checks already owned by the tests.
